chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan from Yusuf ibn Aqil from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
The slaughtered meat of one who professes the word of Islam, fasts, and prays is lawful for you, provided he mentions the name of Allah over it.

This does not contradict the earlier reports for two reasons: the first is that he who sets up war and enmity against the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not truly profess the word of Islam, but rather professes the word of disbelief, and is excluded from what the report encompasses.
The second reason is that it may be attributed to the state of precautionary piety (Taqiyyah).
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of those who hate the Ahl al-Bayt lawful to eat if they pray and fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the general permissibility of meat slaughtered by those who perform the basic pillars of Islam, provided they invoke Allah's name. It introduces a critical Shia nuance: those who actively harbor enmity against the Ahl al-Bayt are excluded from this ruling as they are considered to have left the fold of Islam, while others may be included under the principle of Taqiyyah, where their outward profession of Islam is accepted despite potential inner concealment.
